name: Approximation Algorithms
description:
Many interesting optimization problems are NP-hard, so we cannot hope to find an efficient algorithm for them. But what can we do then when we need to solve them? 

In this course, we will study algorithms for such problems that are efficient and still compute provably good solutions: approximation algorithms. We will see rigorous mathematical analyses so that we are certain that even for the very worst possible inputs they behave as we claim.

We will use a flipped classroom format: there will be several short videos uploaded in Moodle before each lecture. During the lectures, we will discuss their content and answer your questions.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge about (combinatorial) optimization like linear programming, duality, and algorithms for shortest path and maximum flow
